key_insight: For scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing, the best quantum instruction set architecture is a mid-level abstraction: local logical operations balance control complexity with cryogenic hardware limits.
engineering_relevance: This work gives concrete guidance for designing the classical control stack and instruction interface so future superconducting and topological quantum processors can scale without exceeding thermal and routing constraints.
method: Introduced ARIES, a hierarchy of quantum instruction set abstraction levels.
Built an end-to-end, cycle-accurate evaluation toolflow with a classical driver and hardware engine simulator.
Benchmarked eight quantum applications on superconducting and topological qubit platforms.
evidence_signal: The evaluation shows physical-level instructions exceed dilution refrigerator thermal budgets by orders of magnitude, while canonical-level abstractions underestimate routing congestion and execution time.
watch_item: Results depend on the assumed cryogenic platform and simulator models, so real hardware integration may expose additional latency, routing, or thermal overheads.
paper_title: Architecting Instruction Execution for Scalable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
